name: Binary Search Divide and Conquer
explanation: Binary search repeatedly divides a sorted search space in half, achieving logarithmic O(log N) search time.
learning_objectives: Shrink left and right bounds correctly
common_misconceptions: Off-by-one errors when setting left = mid vs left = mid + 1
Applying binary search on unsorted sequences

no_hint.message: Your binary search boundary management is progressing well.
no_hint.next_step: Check your termination condition (left <= right vs left < right).
no_hint.reflection_question: What happens when left and right point to the same index?

concept.message: Binary search cuts the search domain in half at every step by checking the middle element.
concept.next_step: Compare the middle value with your target to decide which half to discard.
concept.reflection_question: How many comparisons does binary search take for an array of 1,000 elements?

guided.next_step: If target < arr[mid], move right to mid - 1. If target > arr[mid], move left to mid + 1.
guided.reflection_question: Why is left + (right - left) // 2 preferred over (left + right) // 2 in languages with fixed integer types?

pseudocode.message:
left = 0, right = length - 1
WHILE left <= right:
    mid = left + (right - left) // 2
    IF arr[mid] == target: RETURN mid
    ELSE IF arr[mid] < target: left = mid + 1
    ELSE: right = mid - 1
RETURN -1
pseudocode.next_step: Implement the binary search loop in your programming language.
pseudocode.reflection_question: What condition guarantees that target is not present in the array?

full_solution.message: Binary search checks the middle element of a sorted array to discard half the search space per iteration in O(log N) time.
full_solution.next_step: Test edge cases like single-element arrays and targets smaller or larger than all elements.
full_solution.reflection_question: How can binary search be adapted to find the first occurrence of duplicate elements?

reflection_questions: Why does binary search achieve logarithmic O(log N) efficiency?
How do you ensure mid calculation does not cause an infinite loop when left and right are adjacent?
pseudocode:
low = 0, high = N - 1
WHILE low <= high:
    mid = (low + high) / 2
    IF A[mid] == target: RETURN mid
    IF A[mid] < target: low = mid + 1
    ELSE: high = mid - 1
RETURN -1

complexity.time: O(log N) - Logarithmic search space reduction
